speaker: presidenta
text: Good afternoon, the Vice-President and I welcome you to our press conference.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The Governing Council is committed to setting monetary policy to ensure that inflation stabilises at our two per cent target in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In line with this commitment, we today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The war in the Middle East is generating inflation pressures, and the decision to raise rates is robust across a range of scenarios mapping out how the shock might evolve and affect the medium-term outlook for the euro area.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: In the baseline of the new Eurosystem staff projections, headline inflation is expected to average 3.0 per cent in 2026, 2.3 per cent in 2027 and 2.0 per cent in 2028.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: For inflation excluding energy and food, the baseline foresees an average of 2.5 per cent in 2026 and 2027 and 2.2 per cent in 2028.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Compared with March, staff have revised up their baseline projection for inflation in 2026 and 2027 owing to a higher path for energy prices, which, to some extent, is expected to feed into food, goods and services inflation.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The baseline sees economic growth at an average of 0.8 per cent in 2026, 1.2 per cent in 2027 and 1.5 per cent in 2028.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: This is a downward revision for 2026 and 2027, reflecting a more pronounced impact of the war on commodity markets, real incomes and confidence.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The outlook remains uncertain, with upside risks for inflation and downside risks for economic growth.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The full implications of the war for medium-term inflation and growth will depend on the intensity and duration of the energy price shock, as well as the scale of its indirect and second-round effects.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: This uncertainty is also reflected in the broad range of outcomes for inflation and growth in the updated illustrative scenarios put together by Eurosystem staff.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: These will be published with the staff projections on our website.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: With today’s decision, we remain well positioned to navigate the uncertainty caused by the war.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We will closely monitor the situation and follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach to determining the appropriate monetary policy stance.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In particular, our interest rate decisions will be based on our assessment of the inflation outlook and the risks surrounding it, in light of the incoming economic and financial data, as well as the dynamics of underlying inflation and the strength of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are not pre-committing to a particular rate path.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The decisions taken today are set out in a press release available on our website.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I will now outline in more detail how we see the economy and inflation developing and will then explain our assessment of financial and monetary conditions.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Adjusting for a temporary factor in Ireland, the euro area economy grew in the first quarter, supported by domestic demand and exports.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Yet the war in the Middle East is weighing on activity and surveys are pointing to a slowdown, especially in services.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Manufacturing has held up so far.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In part, this is because firms have been building up stocks to cope with supply chain pressures.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It also reflects higher defence spending.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The labour market remains resilient.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Unemployment, at 6.3 per cent in April, remains close to historical lows.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The first quarter saw additional jobs being created, although at a slower pace than in the last quarter of 2025.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Labour demand has cooled further, and firms and households expect the labour market to weaken.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Looking ahead, staff now expect domestic demand to be weaker than they projected in March as the war weighs on confidence and higher energy costs erode real incomes.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: At the same time, household balance sheets are solid overall, and consumption should remain the main driver of growth.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Higher energy costs and lower confidence will dent private investment in the short run, but it should be underpinned by firms investing in new digital technologies.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Governments spending more on defence and infrastructure should continue to support public investment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: These factors are expected to provide some cushioning against the fallout from the war.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The Governing Council highlights the urgent need to strengthen the euro area economy while maintaining sound public finances.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Fiscal sustainability is a crucial anchor for broader economic stability.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Fiscal responses to the energy price shock should be temporary, targeted and tailored, as emphasised in the European Commission’s 2026 European Semester Spring Package.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Reforms to enhance the euro area’s growth potential and accelerate the energy transition to reduce reliance on fossil fuels are more vital than ever.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Completing the savings and investments union is key to funding innovation, supporting the green and digital transitions and improving productivity.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The digital euro and tokenised wholesale central bank money will enhance Europe’s strategic autonomy, competitiveness and financial integration, and will boost innovation in payments.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It is thus essential to swiftly adopt the Regulation on the establishment of the digital euro.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Simplifying and harmonising rules across the EU’s Single Market will help European firms grow faster.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation rose to 3.2 per cent in May, from 3.0 per cent in April.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Energy price inflation ticked up to 10.9 per cent, after 10.8 per cent in April, while food price inflation fell from 2.4 per cent to 2.0 per cent.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation excluding energy and food picked up to 2.5 per cent, from 2.2 per cent in April, as goods inflation edged up to 0.9 per cent and services inflation increased from 3.0 per cent to 3.5 per cent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Domestic cost pressures eased in the first quarter, supported by slower growth in wages and profits.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: The ECB’s wage tracker and surveys on wage expectations continue to indicate that wage growth should ease over the year.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: However, it is becoming more expensive for firms to source other inputs and they therefore expect to put up their selling prices.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Moreover, some indicators of underlying inflation have already been driven higher by the energy shock.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation expectations over shorter horizons remain well above levels before the outbreak of the war in the Middle East.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: At the same time, most measures of longer-term inflation expectations stand at around 2 per cent, supporting the stabilisation of inflation around target in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The increase in energy prices will lift inflation further over the summer and keep it well above target into the first half of 2027.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: It will also have an impact on food, goods and services inflation.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation should then return to target in the second half of 2027, supported by falling energy prices and slower increases in other prices.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: However, the war in the Middle East remains a major source of uncertainty.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The longer energy prices stay high, the more likely they are to drive up broader inflation through indirect and second-round effects.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: We will therefore closely monitor the size and persistence of the energy price increase, and how it feeds through to price and wage-setting, inflation expectations and overall economic dynamics.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The risks to the growth outlook are to the downside, mainly owing to the war in the Middle East, which has added to the volatile global policy environment.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: Prolonged disruption of energy supplies could increase energy prices further and for longer than currently expected.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: These factors would erode real incomes even more and make firms and households more reluctant to invest and spend.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The drag on growth would intensify if the closure of major shipping routes were to cause acute shortages of key inputs that forced euro area firms to curtail output.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: A worsening of global financial market sentiment or a tighter supply of credit could dampen demand.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Additional frictions in international trade could also further disrupt supply chains, reduce exports and weaken consumption and investment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Other geopolitical tensions, in particular Russia’s unjustified war against Ukraine, remain a major source of uncertainty.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: By contrast, growth could turn out to be higher if the economy and energy markets were to adapt more quickly than expected to the disruption caused by the war in the Middle East or if the war was resolved promptly and sustainably.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Moreover, planned defence and infrastructure spending, reforms to enhance productivity and euro area firms adopting new technologies may drive up growth by more than expected.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: A deeper integration of the Single Market could also boost growth beyond current expectations.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: If energy prices were to rise by more and for longer than currently expected, euro area inflation would increase further.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: This could be reinforced and become more persistent if higher energy prices were to spill over by more than expected to other prices and to wages, if longer-term inflation expectations were to rise in response, or if global supply chains were disrupted more broadly.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Ongoing trade tensions could also give rise to more fragmented global supply chains, curtail the supply of critical raw materials and worsen capacity constraints in the euro area economy.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Extreme weather events, and the unfolding climate and nature crises more broadly, could drive up food prices by more than expected.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: By contrast, inflation could turn out to be somewhat lower if the economic effects of the war in the Middle East proved to be more short-lived than currently expected or if indirect or second-round effects proved less pronounced than anticipated.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: More volatile and risk-averse financial markets could weigh on demand and thereby lower inflation as well.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: Financial conditions are broadly unchanged since our last meeting but remain tighter than before the war.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The cost of issuing market-based debt rose to 4.0 per cent in April, from 3.9 per cent in March.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Bank lending rates for firms remained at 3.6 per cent in April and mortgage rates at 3.4 per cent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The annual growth rate of bank lending to firms increased to 3.4 per cent in April, from 3.2 per cent in March, while the growth rate of corporate bond issuance rose to 4.6 per cent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Mortgage lending in April again grew by 3.0 per cent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In line with our monetary policy strategy, the Governing Council thoroughly assessed the links between monetary policy and financial stability.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Euro area banks are resilient, supported by strong capital and liquidity ratios, solid asset quality and robust profitability.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: However, a sudden, sharp drop in asset prices, potentially amplified by the non-bank financial sector and deteriorating asset quality, particularly in energy and trade-sensitive sectors, would pose risks to financial stability.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: These risks increase the longer the current geopolitical conflicts last.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Macroprudential policy remains the first line of defence against the build-up of financial vulnerabilities, enhancing resilience and preserving macroprudential space.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The Governing Council today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: We are committed to setting monetary policy to ensure that inflation stabilises at our two per cent target in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We will follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach to determining the appropriate monetary policy stance.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Our interest rate decisions will be based on our assessment of the inflation outlook and the risks surrounding it, in light of the incoming economic and financial data, as well as the dynamics of underlying inflation and the strength of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are not pre-committing to a particular rate path.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In any case, we stand ready to adjust all of our instruments within our mandate to ensure that inflation stabilises sustainably at our medium-term target and to preserve the smooth functioning of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are now ready to take your questions.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Thank you very much for your questions and thank you for greeting the three of us and particularly Boris, our new Vice-President.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The decision that we took today to raise by 25 basis points our three interest rates was a unanimous decision, without reservation.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: We did not discuss or debate any other alternative proposal, and the one that was predicated on the Eurosystem staff projections and the recommendations of our Chief Economist was unanimously endorsed.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: No discussion of others.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Our reaction function has been very steady, repeated over the course of time, and I hope I will not offend you by repeating yet again that given the level of uncertainty that we are facing, we will decide on a meeting-by-meeting basis.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We will be data-dependent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: There will be no preset rate path in our considerations.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And as a result of that, it will be what it will be.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Now, this is not much by way of forward guidance but, as you know, under the present circumstances there is no such justification for the decisions that we are making and that we will make in the future.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I think I would add one thing, because I’ve read here and there that the ECB will make an “insurance decision”, it will be an insurance matter, it will be a pre-emptive rate decision.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: It’s not at all the way we had our discussions, really.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Our discussions were predicated on, obviously, the major energy shock that we have observed since the beginning of March, that is enduring longer than what was expected by geopolitical experts, and which we’re beginning to see broadening throughout the economy, with direct costs being obvious, with indirect costs also showing up and, as I said, we will be monitoring attentively any further consequences of this major energy shock.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: A second response in relation to this insurance allegation of ours, which it was not: we have updated our scenarios, but if you remember from last time around we had two scenarios, which we published.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We will be publishing a third scenario – that will be available on our website – which we have decided to call the milder scenario.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So staff from the Eurosystem have worked on the update of the adverse and the severe scenarios, but they have also worked on a milder scenario in order to be on both sides of the baseline.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And the decision that we took today to increase by 25 basis points all our interest rates is robust across the three scenarios: the two updated adverse and severe, but also the milder scenario, which obviously is more positive and something that we should not neglect, but which is at this point in time unlikely to materialise.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: But we still thought that it was our duty to look at both sides.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And on all accounts, our decision stands.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And if we were not taking that very obvious monetary policy decision, then at the end of the medium term, that we look out for for projection purposes, we would be north of our target.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: So I hope I have covered your question.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: On the services inflation, as you will have seen, it has moved from 3% to 3.5%, which is a significant increase.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Now obviously what we need to understand better is what is under the skin of that increase and how we can distinguish between what is the direct and indirect consequence of the energy prices’ significant increase or whether there is something else.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: At this point in time we cannot yet say whether this significant increase in services prices is attributable exclusively to direct, or to direct and indirect consequences.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: What we are confident in though is that we are not seeing yet second round-effects, which would be largely attributable to wages, which play a significant contribution in the production of services.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But I’m saying again that we will be monitoring closely all that in the months to come.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Now you asked me where we stand, and I just want to take you back to a speech that I gave back in March, which I know you’ve been following.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It was my speech to the ECB Watchers.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In March, at the ECB Watchers Conference, I distinguished between three different situations, which are an analytical frame in and of itself, if you will.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So I’m not going to consider that one is exactly scenario X, Y or Z. But I said, first of all, if the shock is limited and short-lived, it’s a case where we see through.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Now, obviously, we do not find ourselves in this situation because we have decided and we think that it’s a monetary policy that stands firmly on its own and that is robust across all scenarios, so we are not in that “Let’s see through; it’s going to be short-lived and small” situation.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The second situation that I referred to is where the shock produces a large, though not too persistent, overshoot, in which case a measured adjustment of policy is needed.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The third case that I referred to in that ECB Watchers speech is the situation where we expect inflation to deviate significantly and durably from target, in which case the response must be appropriately forceful.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: So I’ll leave it to you to decide which of the three.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I’ve already eliminated case number one, which is clearly not a situation where it’s short-lived and rather small.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: This is not the case.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The decision we’ve made is not a forceful decision either, right?
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Twenty-five basis points is a decision which clearly is a signal and is necessary given the economic situation that we have, given the uncertainty that we are navigating, given the inflation outlook that we have and the projections that have been produced by the Eurosystem staff.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: To the risk of disappointing you, we have not discussed the neutral rate nor the range of neutral rate.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: As you know, there is a lot of work that has been done by staff in that respect, who have given a range within which the neutral rate would be located.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Philip Lane has discussed that extensively in a speech recently.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But we have not debated our positioning with reference to the neutral rate, which I’ll remind you is a bit difficult to actually assess precisely because we are not in a situation where there are no shocks -- which is typically what you need to have as an environment within which you determine where you are neutral, because you don’t stimulate and you don’t restrict.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So this was not debated at all by the Governing Council.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Everybody has to do what they have to do.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Our job is price stability.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And our job is to apply the strategy review principles that we have agreed.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Our job is to follow carefully the reaction function that you are all familiar with and that we try to be as transparent about as possible so that we are predictable.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And in the face of that, frankly, given the numbers we have, given the inflation outlook, given the risk to the upside on inflation, given the robustness of the decision against and across all scenarios – the bad one, the very bad one and the not so bad one – and the fact that it holds in all circumstances, and if you add to that the fact that our growth forecast as revised is 0.8% – minus 0.1 percentage points relative to March – and 1.2% next year and 1.5% the following year, it’s not as if we are in an environment where growth is absent or under significant threat.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: A lot more can be done by structural reforms, by encouraging a European market that has no obstacles to trade, savings and investments union and so on and so forth, and we encourage that very strongly in our monetary policy statement.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Of course we should not be complacent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I think that’s a recurrent principle that we should always apply, as we should apply the principles of being data-dependent, being analytical and rigorous about the analysis that we do of all the numbers that we receive.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And this is what the Eurosystem staff have done and this is what will be done going forward by the ECB staff when they produce the next projections.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So it’s not an issue of complacency.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And honestly, I don’t like to brag and I’m not full of vanity, but I would hasten to add that having maintained inflation pretty much at target over the last 12 months, we have not been complacent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We have done our job and we will continue doing so.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: On your second question, the characterisation of robustness of the decision is obviously helpful when you do scenarios across the board.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So if we had done adverse and severe scenarios and then decided it was robust, of course it is robust.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But we decided on purpose to do scenarios on both sides of the baseline.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And even in the milder scenario, the 25-basis-point cut is completely warranted and justified.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: So this is what we’ve done.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: With reference to the baseline, first of all, I have not compared and we have not gone into the exercise of comparing the baseline with the adverse or the severe scenario at this point in time.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We have updated our baseline both on the account of inflation and on the account of growth as well, with the caveat of Ireland, which is a case in point of international companies organising their business in such a way that it impacts, in an interesting way, the Irish numbers.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So what we have done is that we’ve updated the baseline, and I think the best thing that can be done is to compare the adverse scenario prepared in March with the adverse scenario prepared in June.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I think that is more relevant than baseline versus last-time-around adverse.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And, as I told you in the earlier phase of our discussions today, we are beginning to see a broadening of inflation throughout the economy, and that is obviously in terms of direct effects, but also in terms of indirect effects.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Not yet at this point, in the front of the second-round effects, but we are going to be extremely attentive.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And when we see, for instance, that the delivery times, that the smoothness of supply is beginning to be impaired, obviously we will be attentive to those ancillary indicators that would help us understand where it is heading.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: One more point, because I did speak about wages earlier: we do include a level of second-round effects in our projections, obviously, and the projections that we have for the three years 2026, 2027 and 2028 all anticipate compensation per employee at 3.2%, which in and of itself, if you compare that with the projections that we have on inflation, justifies the fact that the net income of workers will actually be positive and would lead to assume that consumption not only will continue to be the main driver of growth as it is, but will continue to grow probably more than other factors.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We see other factors to fuel growth going forward.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Yes, I did say that it’s not an insurance policy interest rate decision, simply because it’s a good monetary policy interest rate decision.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: When you have the latest reading at 3.2%, when you have the inflation outlook over our target, peaking in the end of 2026, continuing to be over target throughout most of 2027, returning to 2% in the autumn of 2027 and being at target in 2028, on the basis of market curves and all the rest of it, it is pretty obvious that we have to make a decision and that it is a sensible monetary policy decision.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: So I don’t need to characterise it as credibility, insurance or anything else for that matter.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It’s a monetary policy decision that stands and that is, as we say in the monetary policy statement, robust across all scenarios, including the mild one.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are of course delighted that Croatia is a member of the euro area, and I and all Governing Council members and members of the Executive Board are delighted to have the Croatian National Bank – I was going to say former governor – being now a member of the Executive Board and the new Vice-President of the ECB.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It’s a great representation and it brings diversity amongst the group and it’s really a blessing that Boris has joined us.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But turning to inflation, of course we are concerned about inflation, but we are not just concerned about inflation in one Member State or the other because our job at the ECB is to look at the whole of the euro area.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And our concern, as I said earlier on, is that we see the energy price inflation – 10.9% at the moment – broadening throughout the economy, which is why we are making this decision today.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Broadening inflation outlook, underlying inflation – all of that point in the direction of having to make a decision of increasing interest rates.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: So because our mission and our mandate is to restore price stability, we make those decisions and we are driven by that objective – price stability.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: As I said, our mission and our mandate is price stability.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We have defined price stability, for our strategy review and our purpose of making decisions, at 2% in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: When you see inflation picking up in the way it does, broadening throughout the economy, when you see inflation outlook north of that 2% target and only returning to 2% at the end of our projection horizon, when you see risks to the upside, to us this is inflation that needs to be taken into account and that needs to be addressed.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: So I don’t know what other governors in whatever publications or interviews you refer to allege that it would be higher inflation, but we do have inflation that is too high for our citizens, that is too high for the purpose of price stability as well, and we will address that because our commitment is price stability.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Your second question was about the risks resulting from this decision.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: First of all, I would observe that the main risk would be not to take that kind of decision, because if you let inflation start running out without control, then it becomes a much more difficult situation to bring it back to the level of price stability that we have defined.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: So the good decision was actually to raise interest rates, to commit and to deliver on price stability, so that people will make their investment decisions, their employment decisions and their wage negotiations decisions in the light of that commitment to restore price stability, as we will.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: In terms of inflation expectations, we look at three categories of expectations.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We look at market-based measures, we look at survey-based measures and we look at consumers’ expectations.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And we try to understand exactly where those expectations stand between the short term and the medium term that is relevant for our monetary policy decisions.
